concerns.text: FR-004 uses a Median Absolute Deviation (MAD) rule for outlier removal, whereas the idea specifies ±3 σ. This methodological change is not justified and drifts from the original research plan, potentially affecting reproducibility of results.

FR-011 requires validation of the sign of mean SHAP values against a curated literature lookup table. The original idea only demanded that SHAP direction match known physical trends; the lookup‑table requirement introduces a new validation step not requested.

SC-004 mandates that at least three features have statistically significant SHAP values (p < 0.05) based on a permutation‑test. The idea never called for significance testing of SHAP values, only for identifying a concise set of important descriptors. This adds an unrequested research question.
SC-005 imposes an execution‑time ceiling of ≤ 6 hours. The idea does not specify any runtime constraint; this is an engineering bound that was not part of the original scope.
SC-007 limits imputed material‑property rows to ≤ 5 % of the dataset. The original idea required median imputation but did not set a quantitative logging threshold, making this an over‑reach.
The NIST Materials Data Repository citation is missing its DOI (shown as empty parentheses). The idea explicitly references a NIST DOI; the spec fails to provide a verifiable external source.

The specification uses both `material_pair_id` (FR-014) and `pairing_id` (Edge Cases) to denote the grouping identifier. This inconsistency can cause traceability and data‑leakage issues, diverging from the clear terminology in the idea.
